A1.justification: Both PDFs describe FAB-PPI by the same authors. Their main text, equations, algorithms, figures, and appendices S1–S6 are readable and support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: Section 5 and Appendix S6 report original simulations and evaluations on six real datasets, measuring estimation error, confidence-interval volume, and empirical coverage.

after.justification: Section 5 and Appendix S6 retain the work's original simulation and real-data results, including estimation error, interval volume, and coverage.

M1.justification: Algorithms 1 and 2 correct the standard-error scaling for the unlabeled mean: Algorithm 1 introduces division by sqrt(N), and Algorithm 2 uses variance normalization N(N−1). This repairs the written finite-sample interval calculation. The rectifier estimator, priors, shrinkage mechanism, and power tuning remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same biased/noisy prediction simulations and AlphaFold, Forest, Galaxies, Healthcare, Genes, and Census tasks. Section 5.2 now identifies AlphaFold explicitly as odds-ratio estimation, but that task and its construction were already documented in v1 Appendix S5.1.

E2.justification: Corresponding experiments retain the same comparator membership: classical inference, PPI, PPI++, their full-uncertainty variants where applicable, and the same FAB prior variants. Figures 1–3 and S6–S13 show no added or removed comparison methods.

E3.justification: The reported sample sizes, random labeled/unlabeled splits, bias and noise settings, nominal error level, and MSE/volume/coverage metrics are unchanged. Both versions use the same large-unlabeled-sample simplification. The new implementation subsection discloses details without reporting a revised experimental protocol.

E4.justification: The bias and noise sweeps, Gaussian-versus-horseshoe comparisons, example intervals in Figure S9, and Forest prior-scale sensitivity analysis in Figure S10 are retained. The Census analysis of bias and labeled sample size is also unchanged.

E5.justification: Experimental repetition counts and uncertainty-reporting practices are unchanged, including 1000 repetitions for the principal studies and 100 for Figures S10 and S12. Neither version adds seeds, confidence bands for experimental averages, or significance tests.

E6.justification: The corresponding experimental figures retain identical plotting content, including numerical curves, example intervals, and comparator rankings. The empirical findings in Sections 5 and S6 are unchanged; the added AlphaFold coverage explanation does not introduce new results.

T1.justification: Appendix S3 substantially revises the horseshoe convergence argument. V1 Lemmas S3.2–S3.3 are replaced by a horseshoe-specific lemma using uniform bounds and Hausdorff convergence, with classical normalized-interval convergence restricted to nonzero rectifiers. V2 separately establishes coverage at zero and discusses its random limiting region; the Gaussian proof also gains the missing zero case. The robustness corollary now concerns full-set convergence, and Section 3.1 corrects the control-variate variance-reduction condition.

C1.justification: The abstract and contribution list retain the same claims: valid Bayes-assisted PPI, improved efficiency when predictions agree with the prior, robustness with heavy-tailed priors, and compatibility with power tuning. The principal contribution and its intended scope remain unchanged.

C2.justification: Appendix S5.1 newly explains AlphaFold's above-nominal coverage in Figure 3 as conservatism introduced by the union-bound construction of the odds-ratio interval. Existing interpretations of prediction bias, horseshoe robustness, prior-scale choices, and computational limitations are retained.

D1.justification: V2 adds a code-repository link and Appendix S5.2, identifying Python, ppi-py for baseline comparisons, and an Intel Core i7-11850H CPU. These are new reproducibility disclosures; the PDFs do not establish a change in the underlying implementation or hardware.

R1.justification: V2 adds Efron (2011) for Tweedie's formula, replacing empty citations in Section 4.1 and Appendix S1.1. The renamed Cortinovis–Caron reference has the same arXiv identifier, and other bibliography updates concern existing works. The positioning relative to PPI and Bayesian PPI remains unchanged.

P1.justification: V2 makes localized explanatory rewrites, clarifies the AlphaFold task, fixes grammar and cross-references, and adds implementation, code, and impact-statement text. The appendix proof organization changes locally, while the overall section sequence and narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: All thirteen figures and both algorithm boxes remain. Figure S5 is reduced in display size, several figures shift within the page flow, captions receive small edits, and the running title is removed. The plotted graphics themselves are unchanged.

improvement.justification: V1's horseshoe convergence lemma asserted classical normalized-interval behavior even at a zero rectifier using an insufficient pointwise argument. V2 restricts that conclusion, supplies a substantially fuller convergence proof, and establishes zero-case coverage separately. Together with the standard-error corrections in both algorithms and new implementation information, these changes substantially strengthen the paper's central theoretical support and the reliability of its stated procedure. The empirical evidence remains unchanged.
